correctness.rationale: The normalized weight has positive mass outside every smaller disk and is integrable for b>0 and all real gamma. Panja's Kraus coefficients telescope on the diagonal to rho*delta_n*x_(n+1)+(1-rho*delta_n)*x_n; the coefficients are bounded (log-convexity of the moments gives omega_(n+1)/omega_n >= rho). Writing r_n=omega_(n+1)/omega_n gives the unique nonzero formal solution normalized at x_0=1, with multiplier 1-r_n+exp(i theta)r_n, never zero for the stated angles. For the moment and its first difference rescale t=u/n, with exponents b and b+1 respectively: the integrands up to sqrt(n) are dominated by an exponentially decreasing function times u^(b-1) or u^b and a fixed power of 1+|log u|; the t>=1/sqrt(n) tails are exponentially small even after rescaling. This gives the two claimed Gamma constants and 1-r_n~b/n. The log of the multiplier modulus minus (1-cos theta)log r_n is O((1-r_n)^2); its sum converges and the finite factors are nonzero. Using the exact telescoping product of r_n gives the stated asymptotic with positive constant. The power-log series test includes divergence at gamma=-b on the critical line. Conjugation gives the other angle; real angles and general off-diagonal operators are excluded. Checked RESULT.md, the recorded quadrature notes in VERIFICATION.md, and the primary Kraus formula; no finite quadrature is needed as a proof or claimed as independently rerun.
